chapter: Later career and The Benny Goodman Story
title: Which came first: Goodman's Carnegie Hall concert or Spirituals to Swing
summary: Wilson says Basie played Carnegie Hall in Spirituals to Swing, and he and Ted Jr. argue over dates with Hammond's concerts and an earlier 1928 concert.

blocks.x: But for the record, I think it should be made clear that that wasn't the first jazz in Carnegie Hall. Count Basie played in Carnegie Hall before Goodman, in a program called "Spiritual Swing." They had the Golden Gate Quartet on there and I think the boogie-woogie pianist, Pete Johnson, Albert Hammond, maybe Leadbelly was on there. And Basie represented the swing. Do you remember that concert?
That's right, yeah.
From spirituals to swing. (Inaudible).
(Inaudible).
I just want to make a point of correction, I just recently made a tape of that concert for Joe

Jones, and it took place the same year but the Spiritual Swing Concert took place in December of 1938 whereas the Goodman Concert took place in January of 1938. So actually it did come a little later.
Are you sure about that? You said Goodman was in January.
And the Spiritual Swing was in December.
Oh, wait a minute. No, '38 and '39. But now there was a big concert --
Wait a minute. You said Spirituals to Swing --
Spirituals of Swing were two concerts in 19 --
Well, Goodman was January 1938.
Right. And the first Spiritual Swing was --
It had to be '37. Because Goodman was January '38.
Right.
Before that would be '37.
Right, but the Spiritual Swing Con-
certs came after that Goodman concert, later that year and the following year in '39.

But there is another concert that took place before both of those, which I can't recall the name of. But I think, Milt, you told me about it. Something maybe as early as 1928. I don't know if it was in Carnegie Hall.
It seems to me the Spirituals to Swing, (inaudible) with Basie and Leadbelly was before the Goodman Concert. Maybe wasn't.

Well, the ones that I have, I just recorded, according to the notes, they were sponsored by John Hammond. According to the notes they took place in two years, they were December of 1938 and December of 1939.
Well, (unintelligible) we can find out whether Goodman was first stuff or Basie, the great jazz band.

There was a jazz concert which took place a good deal before both of them, before 1938. It seems to me it was as early as 1928. I don't know if it was so jazz-oriented as these other two were, it seemed like it had more variety. It seems to me the Jubilee Singers. It seems to me you told me about this once before?
